title: Gottfried van Swieten (Bonn) to Count Cobenzl, 14 Jan and 4 Feb 1759 (ARA Brussels SEG 1236; DECODE R956, R957)

steps.what: DECODE R955-R957 fetched with the session cookie (8 page images, 3 transcriptions); R956 and R957 are this entry.
Web search and local Tomokiyo/cryptiana copies for a printed decipherment.
R955's values applied to the 1759 runs directly and linearly rescaled to 100-442.

Monotone-map annealer (msolve.py) onto a sorted inventory of French units, LM score + per-letter bonus; first runs collapsed onto repeated long words (no multiplicity cap) and a score bug (sum taken as mean).
Synthetic 274-group French text under a random alphabetical table: recovered verbatim once the 2-codes-per-unit cap and bonus 1.5 were set.
8 random starts on the 491 clean 1759 groups; seed 5 gave readable French (la nouvelle convention... souverainete... imperatrice), the others gibberish.
Four DECODE runs with dropped/doubled digits re-read from the images; a separate sign before run 1 dropped.
Seeded polish pass with enlarged inventory drifted to worse keys.
Key corrected by hand run by run against the surrounding clear French (magazins, Contades, Broglio, comte de Pergen); x 438/439, y 441, z 442 close the table.

R956 run 11 re-read against the alphabetical order of the table, after a slip was reported while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list: 'le major (?) general des Liegeois de Vaut' needed 238 = ge ahead of 239 g and 240 ga; by position 238 = g, 294 = lo (after 293 li), 300 between 299 ma and 303 me, giving 'le m[arechal] general des logis de Vaut' (graded I; digits confirmed on the image). key.json/overrides.json: 238 g, 294 lo, 300 marechal?. Officer probably Francois-Eugene de Vault, not verified.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 551 tokens, 152 types, fr-1750-nospace order 4: reading -2.122 per letter; random keys -4.404 (z 12.8); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.493 (mean -2.518, z 13.1); annealer on the real text -2.494. Verdict: pass.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R955 (1757 table, 202-586, read from the decipherment on its own page) stays in swieten1757; R956/R957 (the 1759 table, 100-442, rebuilt ciphertext-only) moved to swieten1759 with msolve.py, dec.py, key.json, overrides.json, runs.txt, validation.tsv.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R957 and R956 linked to cipher/R95x.txt (group transcriptions) and READING.md (both readings); key_file key.json

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): READING.md read per letter: R956 builds French sentences with scattered name groups open; R957 has holes or garbled clauses in two of its four sentences. R957 relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.962 -> 0.597 (estimated); excerpt notes added to both.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b36): DECODE R957 refetched logged in; all four images opened. Image 4 (IMG_R957_I4985_P4) is a contemporary decipherment of the cipher passage on a separate leaf, never opened in the September work; the decipherer wrote 232 above 'France'. Neighbours R954, R958 unrelated.

Decipherment transcribed (R957_decipherment.txt) and aligned group by group with the figures decoded by dec.py: word-for-word agreement once 232 France, 327 oc, 131 ay, 170 cr, 323 o, 440 y, 316 ni are corrected (each at every occurrence; 170 also gives R956 'Crillon', 316 'Dumenil'; 327 and 440 close two order breaks of the alphabetical table). One encipherer's slip (357 for -on in 'supposition'). key.json and overrides.json updated.
R957_reading.md and R957_en.md written in the decipherer's spelling; b17 0.857 plain (was 0.571), 1.0 explicit holes; look-alike share 0. Set read, grade A; class back to read (both documents read).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.122; polyphony 0.0; 2 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.494

outcome.method_basis: The 1759 alphabetical syllabary (R956, R957) was rebuilt by a monotone-map annealer from the ciphertext (seed 5 of 8 gave French), then corrected by hand against the clear French around each run.

gaps.item: R956 name groups 147 100 126 148 (run 4) and 290 313 316 313 373 (run 16, digit division uncertain)
gaps.detail: names read only as letters of the rebuilt table; no decipherment of R956 on the record, one context each

outcome.notes: fraction_read = documents that read. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R957 decoded, not read; class read in part. 23 Oct 2026 (re-read b36): R957's fourth DECODE image is a contemporary decipherment of its cipher passage; aligned with the figures, it corrects seven table values (232 France, 327 oc, 131 ay, 170 cr, 323 o, 440 y, 316 ni; two of the seven order breaks of the table closed) and R957 reads; R956 gains Crillon and Dumenil. Class back to read. The key was rebuilt ciphertext-only before the decipherment was seen; R957's decipherment is a contemporary text found afterwards.

texts.label: R957, ff. 327-328, Bonn, 14 Jan 1759
texts.summary: Gottfried van Swieten at Bonn to Count Cobenzl at Brussels: the new convention leaves the revenues to France while reserving sovereignty to the Empress; the French act on it without any order from the court, causing much ill feeling; on France's behalf the Prince de Croÿ, who has claims to it, has been put in possession of the principality of Moers without the Empress, its sovereign, being told.

reading_review.note: Read from the contemporary decipherment of the cipher passage, a separate leaf filed with the letter (DECODE R957 image 4, never opened before; R957_decipherment.txt), aligned group by group with the figures: they agree word for word once seven values of the rebuilt table are corrected (232 France, 327 oc, 131 ay, 170 cr, 323 o, 440 y, 316 ni), each holding at every occurrence; one encipherer's slip at 'supposition'. b17 on the body 0.857 plain (was 0.571), 1.0 explicit holes. Excerpt: the cipher passage in full; the clear letter is on the DECODE images.

texts.label: R956, ff. 344-345, Bonn, 4 Feb 1759
texts.summary: On Soubise's army: no magazines are being made except at the expense of the exhausted Estates of the Empire, the principle being to keep the King's army without its costing a sou; the contributions of Guelders paid for his army and money was sent to Contades' army for winter quarters.
texts.note: Excerpt only: the cipher runs are given in full, the clear text around them in extract; the full letter is on the DECODE images (R956).

outcome.fraction_read_source: Re-read b36, 23 Oct 2026: both documents read (R956 343 groups, R957 210 groups, cipher/*.txt), so tokens of documents that read / all = 553/553. Within them about 9 groups of R956 stay open (147 100 126 148; 290 313 316 313 373).
